patients.summary: Administrative assistant with limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis on mycophenolate from outside rheumatology, Raynaud and GERD, who joined in 2022. Esophageal dysmotility worked up by GI in 2024; last seen December 2024, after which SSc-associated pulmonary arterial hypertension was diagnosed and treated by cardiology and reached the chart only as outside letters.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT

54F transferring care after her longtime PCP retired. Brought her bottles.

Scleroderma, limited type (CREST), diagnosed around 2016 by rheumatology. Fingers blanch in cold and with stress - has had that for years before the SSc diagnosis. Wears gloves Oct-April, amlodipine helps. Rheum keeps her on mycophenolate 1000 bid, labs through their office every few months, sees them once a year in the fall. Reflux for years, omeprazole 40 every morning, no heartburn breaking through on it. Swallowing fine. No SOB, no cough, walks the dog most evenings without trouble.

PSH: lap chole 2010. R carpal tunnel release this June, healed, numbness gone.
Meds: omeprazole 40 daily, amlodipine 5 daily, mycophenolate 1000 bid (rheum), ASA 81 daily - not sure who started the aspirin or why, has just always been on it.
All: NKDA
FH: mother RA, father HTN, sister Hashimoto.
SH: married, admin assistant at a school district office. Never smoked. Wine once or twice a month.

Exam: well appearing. Skin tightening over the fingers distal to the MCPs, no digital ulcers, nailfolds unremarkable to the eye. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear, no crackles at the bases. Abd soft, healed lap scars. No edema. R palm scar well healed.

A/P
1. Limited cutaneous SSc - per rheum, continue MMF. Will ask them to cc us on letters.
2. Raynaud - stable on amlodipine 5.
3. GERD - controlled, continue omeprazole.
4. HM: prior records requested (she thinks colonoscopy 2019 was clean, Pap 2018). Mammogram ordered. Labs today incl A1c, TSH, one-time HCV/HIV. Flu and shingles vaccine at a nurse visit next month - recombinant zoster is fine on MMF.

RTC 6 mo.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Margaret, your blood counts, kidney and liver tests, cholesterol, sugar and thyroid all came back normal, and the hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. Nothing to change. Good to meet you.

reports.text: Specimen adequate, transformation zone present. Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV not detected.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
38 pages received from previous PCP. Abstracted:
- Screening colonoscopy 04/2019: normal to the cecum, good prep, no polyps; repeat at 10 years.
- Pap with HPV cotest 05/2018: NILM, HPV negative.
- Tdap 02/2016.
- Lap cholecystectomy 2010; R carpal tunnel release 06/2022 (op note included).
- Rheumatology letters 2019-2021 on file confirming limited SSc on mycophenolate.
Filed to media; PCP to review.

documents.title: Nurse visit - immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu 0.5 mL IM L deltoid. Shingrix dose 1 0.5 mL IM R deltoid. Screening questions negative, aware of possible soreness and fatigue for a day or two. Dose 2 due in 2-6 months, scheduled for January. Tolerated well.

reports.text: Bilateral CC and MLO views with tomosynthesis. Breasts are scattered areas of fibroglandular density. No suspicious mass, calcifications or architectural distortion. No prior outside comparison available.

documents.title: Rheumatology follow-up letter
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology practice
Date of visit: 11/17/2022

Dear Colleague,

Thank you for taking over Mrs. Cummings's primary care. I saw her for her yearly review of limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis.

She is doing well. Raynaud attacks are typical for her for the season and manageable with gloves, hand warmers and amlodipine. No digital ulcers. Reflux is controlled. She denies dyspnea, cough or dysphagia.

Examination: BP and pulse normal. Sclerodactyly limited to the fingers, unchanged from last year; no pitting scars or ulcers. Lungs clear. Heart sounds normal.

Monitoring labs today: CBC and comprehensive panel within normal limits.

Impression: limited cutaneous SSc, stable.
Plan: continue mycophenolate mofetil 1000 mg twice daily (we will continue to prescribe and monitor every 3 months). Continue amlodipine 5 mg. Return in one year.

Medications: mycophenolate mofetil 1000 mg BID, amlodipine 5 mg daily, omeprazole 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Sincerely,
Rheumatology

documents.title: Nurse visit - Shingrix #2
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Second Shingrix given IM L deltoid. Said the first one knocked her out for an evening, nothing more. Series complete, immunization record updated.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Routine recheck. Rough Raynaud winter, a few more attacks in Jan when the office heat was off for a week, color comes back with warming. No sores on her fingertips. Reflux quiet. No trouble swallowing, no breathing complaints. Saw rheum in Nov, letter reviewed.

O: vitals as charted. Fingers cool, sclerodactyly unchanged, capillary refill brisk, no ulcers. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear throughout. No edema.

A/P: SSc/Raynaud/GERD all stable on current regimen. Talked about keeping the core warm, not just hands. Annual physical in the fall.

documents.title: Refill amlodipine
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, the pharmacy says my amlodipine is out of refills. Could you send a new one? I have about 5 left. Thank you, Margaret

documents.title: RE: Refill amlodipine
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hi Margaret, a 90 day supply with refills was sent to your pharmacy this morning.

reports.text: Liquid-based preparation. Satisfactory for evaluation; endocervical component present. Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV not detected.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL EXAM - 55F

Interval: no new problems. Raynaud fine this summer. GERD controlled on omeprazole. Still on MMF via rheum, last letter 11/22, next rheum visit in Nov. Walking the dog daily, no exertional limits. No swallowing trouble.

ROS otherwise negative. PHQ-2 0.

Meds unchanged: omeprazole 40, amlodipine 5, MMF 1000 bid, ASA 81. NKDA.

Exam: Vitals reviewed. HEENT normal. Thyroid normal size. Heart regular rate, normal S1 S2. Lungs clear. Breast exam deferred to imaging per her preference. Abdomen benign. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix normal, Pap with HPV collected. Skin: sclerodactyly as before. Ext without edema.

Plan
- Pap/HPV sent.
- PCV20 today given immunosuppression.
- Mammogram ordered.
- Colonoscopy up to date (2019, next 2029).
- CBC, CMP, lipids.
- Flu and updated COVID when the fall supply is in - nurse visit in October.
- Continue current meds. Recheck in spring.

documents.title: Physical results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Margaret - Pap is normal and HPV negative, so the next one can wait 5 years. Blood counts, chemistries and cholesterol are all in a good range. Talk soon.

documents.title: Nurse visit - fall vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: 2023-24 flu vaccine to L arm and 2023-24 Pfizer COVID to R arm. No prior reactions. Observed 15 minutes, left feeling well.

reports.text: Bilateral screening views with tomosynthesis, compared with 10/2022. Scattered fibroglandular densities. No new mass, suspicious calcification or distortion. Stable appearance.

documents.title: Rheumatology annual letter
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology practice - visit 11/14/2023

Re: Margaret Cummings, DOB 05/01/1968

Annual review, limited cutaneous SSc. Uneventful year. Raynaud is seasonal and controlled; no ulceration. No breathlessness, cough or swallowing difficulty reported. Reflux controlled on PPI.

Exam: skin score stable, changes confined to the fingers. Chest clear. Cardiac exam normal.

Labs: CBC and CMP unremarkable.

Plan: no change. Mycophenolate mofetil 1000 mg twice daily, quarterly monitoring labs through our office. See again in 12 months.

Current medications: mycophenolate mofetil 1000 mg BID; amlodipine 5 mg daily; omeprazole 40 mg daily; aspirin 81 mg daily. NKDA.

Rheumatology
